source_snapshot.procedure:
【Before Test】
    1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
    2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).

    【During Test】
    1. Access Redfish Endpoint:
        Access the Redfish API endpoint /redfish/v1/Systems/1/LogServices/PlatformLog.
2. Check Date and Service Status:
        Verify that the "DateTimeLocalOffset" and "DateTime" match the BMC web interface.
        Ensure that "ServiceEnabled" is set to true.
3. Customize BMC Event Log:
        Log in to the BMC from the web interface.
        Go to "Events" → "Event Log".
        Open "Customize Table" and make sure all columns are selected, then click "OK".
4. Generate Events:
        Ensure that the system log contains at least one info, one warning, and one error event.
5.  Access Redfish Log Entries:
        Access the Redfish API endpoint /redfish/v1/Systems/1/LogServices/PlatformLog/Entries.
6. Compare Entries:
        Compare the entries in the "PlatformLog Entries" with the BMC web "Event Log".
        Verify that "Severity," "Source," "Message," "Created," "CommonEventID," "Serviceable," and "TotalSequenceNumber" match.

    【After Test】
    1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
    2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.
source_snapshot.criteria:
Critical content in Redfish and the WebGUI log should match.
    Log entries with different severities (OK, Warning, Critical) should be verified and matched between Redfish and the BMC web interface.

deepseek_columns.ai_commands: ipmitool -I lanplus -C 17 -H "$BMC_IP" -U "$BMC_USER" -P "$BMC_PASS" mc info 2>&1 | grep -i syslog; echo ---; bash -c 'cat /etc/rsyslog.d/*.conf 2>/dev/null; grep -rhE "^\*\." /etc/rsyslog* 2>/dev/null' | grep remote; echo ---; ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no "$DUT_USER@$DUT_IP" 'grep -iE "redfish|syslog|critical" /var/log/syslog | tail -40' 2>&1
deepseek_columns.ai_logs_output: return BMC syslog config + remote rsyslog matches so user confirms critical Redfish/WebGUI content reached the remote syslog. No RISK (read-only).

original_test_intent: Unresolved in the Master: Items and the referenced Script identify a Remote Syslog forwarding test, while every Procedure and Criteria checkpoint validates only local BMC Redfish PlatformLog versus BMC WebGUI event-log equality across time, status, severity and named fields.
original_method: The preserved body queries `/redfish/v1/Systems/1/LogServices/PlatformLog`, checks BMC date/time offset and service state, displays all Web Event Log columns, obtains info/warning/error records and compares seven fields between local Redfish entries and local WebGUI. It never names, configures or observes a remote syslog receiver.
manual_activity: No DUT or collector execution is permitted until engineering selects or splits the test purpose and reviews the internal Script. Afterward an owner must approve any logging configuration and event stimuli; automation may gather complete local/receiver evidence for the chosen checkpoints, but local parity and remote delivery must retain separate results.
required_inputs: Engineer decision whether this Source Identity validates remote forwarding, local Redfish/WebGUI parity or both as independently accepted checkpoints

For local parity: discovered supported PlatformLog URI, WebUI field authority, complete pagination, `DateTime`/`DateTimeLocalOffset` meaning, field normalization and mapping between info/warning/error and OK/Warning/Critical
Safe uniquely identifiable stimuli or pre-existing records for each severity, with source/message/Created/CommonEventID/Serviceable/TotalSequenceNumber expectations and concurrency boundaries

For remote delivery: exact collector identity/address, UDP/TCP/TLS port/transport, certificate/authentication, facility/severity filters, message format, hostname/source/time mapping and loss/order/duplicate/latency criteria
Pinned immutable accessible internal `remote-syslog` Script revision, checksum, dependencies and step-by-step scope/safety review
Protected BMC/host/collector credentials, trusted identities, maintenance approval, original configuration snapshot, rollback, receiver cleanup and alternate access
safety_requirements: Do not infer remote delivery from local Redfish or WebGUI records, BMC configuration text or a host-side grep. The same uniquely identified event must be observed at the independent approved receiver for remote coverage.
Do not clear BMC, host or receiver logs. Establish stable IDs/counts/timestamps and preserve full baseline evidence so existing events and first-failure data remain auditable.
Do not use `StrictHostKeyChecking=no`, `curl -k`, command-line passwords or unscoped local configuration reads. Pin endpoint/host identity and use protected least-privilege credentials.
Do not assume `/Systems/1/LogServices/PlatformLog` exists or silently substitute a Manager/OEM resource. Discover supported links and obtain engineer approval for any semantic mapping.

Do not create warning/error events until each stimulus is demonstrated reversible, bounded and non-incident-producing with defined abort/recovery; existing events are acceptable only when uniquely attributable and within the approved window.

Do not execute the inaccessible internal Script until a pinned revision is available and reviewed for configuration writes, clears, event generation, credentials, receiver target, retries and rollback.

Do not use `tail -40`, grep-only text or configuration presence as completeness proof and do not retry automatically; preserve raw full pages/receiver records and stop on scope ambiguity, wrong destination, unsafe event or evidence loss.
agent_execution_scope: Before the engineer decision, perform document analysis only; do not access the DUT, change forwarding, generate events or invoke the Script.
If local parity is approved, discover trusted resources, capture complete paginated entries and correlate the exact seven fields plus time/status/severity against WebUI for each approved event.

If remote forwarding is approved, separately prove configuration and transport identity and collect receiver-side records for the same event IDs/timestamps, with delivery latency, order, duplication and loss evidence.
Keep local and remote outcomes distinct, preserve all logs, restore approved temporary configuration, never retry event generation automatically and never issue DUT PASS/FAIL.
engineer_actions: Select the authoritative scope or approve two named checkpoints and update the Review-layer acceptance contract without changing the Master source.
Approve canonical local resources/fields/severity normalization and, if applicable, remote collector/transport/message criteria plus safe event stimuli.
Provide and approve a pinned Script revision, supervise configuration/stimuli/recovery and issue separate verdicts for each retained checkpoint.

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: Unfit for either interpretation. `mc info` and local config greps do not prove forwarding; a host `tail -40` is not receiver evidence; none of the commands retrieves the specified PlatformLog fields or WebUI rows. Insecure host-key/credential practices and assumed file locations make literal execution unacceptable.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: No execution command is valid until engineering resolves the target. Then use trusted complete Redfish/WebUI collection for local parity and an independently identified collector capture for remote delivery, sharing only approved uniquely identifiable event stimuli and never substituting one evidence path for the other.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: Remote Syslog title/Script, Systems/1 PlatformLog paths, DateTime/offset, ServiceEnabled, Customize Table, required severities/fields, generic pre-clear, DeepSeek command and 10/0-minute estimates remain preserved as conflicting source evidence.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Split into checkpoint A (local Redfish PlatformLog-to-WebGUI representation parity) and checkpoint B (remote syslog forwarding to an external receiver) unless engineering explicitly retains only one. Correlate the same safe uniquely identified events but judge each endpoint independently.
modernized_recommendation.applicable_platform: The engineer-approved BMC logging architecture, firmware/WebUI implementation and optional remote collector/transport.
modernized_recommendation.supported_version: Record BMC firmware, Redfish/OEM schema, browser, syslog client/receiver and pinned Script revision/checksum.
modernized_recommendation.official_reference: Platform LogService/Web Event Log mapping and remote-syslog forwarding/transport specification plus Project monitoring policy.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Resolves the local-versus-remote target conflict, discovers resources rather than guessing and adds actual receiver evidence where remote coverage is retained.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Local API/UI equality proves no packet delivery; remote receipt proves neither all seven local fields nor WebUI rendering; configuration text proves neither. One checkpoint cannot stand in for the other.
modernized_recommendation.required_inputs: Scope/split decision, local field/event matrix, optional receiver/transport contract, reviewed Script, security, rollback and approval.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Wrong scoping can yield a convincing false PASS; uncontrolled event generation can trigger monitoring; insecure collection can disclose credentials/logs; retries can hide loss by creating duplicates.

project_override_considerations: Project SPEC may split or select one branch, but must record the original Remote Syslog identity and local-only body, actual target/tool, engineer approval, equivalence decision and any unverified branch. A local-only result can never be labeled remote delivery, and a receiver record cannot substitute for the required Redfish/WebGUI field comparison.
expected_evidence: Engineer scope/split decision, exact BMC/firmware identity and pinned reviewed internal Script revision/checksum or explicit alternate method
For local parity: trusted resource discovery, service/date/offset state, full raw paginated entries and WebUI all-column evidence for each approved severity
Canonical per-event mapping of Severity, Source, Message, Created/timezone, CommonEventID, Serviceable and TotalSequenceNumber, including normalization and concurrent-event boundaries
For remote coverage: redacted forwarding configuration, collector/transport/TLS identity and receiver-side raw records for the same event IDs with latency/order/duplicate/loss result
Safe stimulus authorization and timestamps, preserved no-clear baseline, secure command audit and no automatic retry
Restored configuration/collector cleanup, final BMC/receiver health, limitations and engineer-owned separate verdicts

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Items and Script say Remote Syslog, but Procedure and Criteria exclusively compare local Redfish PlatformLog with the BMC WebGUI and provide no receiver, forwarding configuration or delivery criterion. The Procedure's info/warning/error terms also require an approved mapping to Criteria's OK/Warning/Critical.

blocked_analysis.analysis: Remote forwarding and local UI/API representation are different core functions, targets and evidence paths. Choosing one by inference or executing DeepSeek's third method would misstate coverage; engineering must select or split the purpose before execution, so this meets the V3.1 BLOCKED threshold rather than ordinary missing-input readiness.

comparison_to_prior_reviews.deepseek: Rejects YES and its configuration/tail shortcut as proof of either local field parity or external delivery.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.gpt_v2: Changes PACKAGE to BLOCKED because owner-supplied parameters cannot repair the unresolved core target without an engineer scope decision.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.round_02: Adds the missing title/body purpose check, independent receiver boundary and safe event/complete-evidence requirements.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.related_v3_1: Applies the same non-substitution principle as distinct row 832 while preserving this row's separate identity, timing and history.

review_improvement: Prevents local log presence, local host grep or configuration text from being mislabeled as remote-syslog success, and prevents a remote record from concealing incomplete seven-field WebUI/API parity.
independent_technical_reasoning: Redfish and WebGUI are two local representations owned by the BMC; remote syslog is a transport pipeline whose terminal evidence exists on another system. Their failure modes and acceptance evidence are disjoint. Because the source assigns the Remote Syslog identity to a wholly local procedure, the missing item is not merely an IP or package but the authoritative test purpose itself, so review can define both safe branches but cannot select one or execute.
